The Edo State House of Assembly has mourned the death of a 12-year-old boy in a gas explosion at Agbado Market, calling for regulatory guidelines to prevent further incidents.
The member representing Oredo West State Constituency, Richard Edosa, raised the matter as one of urgent public importance during Monday’s plenary in Benin.
Mr Edosa said the explosion injured several others, drawing attention to the dangers associated with gas-related activities. He called for regulatory measures to prevent a recurrence.
Other lawmakers who contributed to the debate sympathised with the victims’ families.
The Speaker, Yekini Idaiye, expressed condolences to the affected families and urged residents to observe safety precautions.
Meanwhile, the House passed a bill seeking to establish the Edo Agency for Education Quality and Accountability.
The proposed agency is expected to strengthen quality assurance and maintain educational standards across the state.

The bill passed after the Committee of the Whole considered it, and the House took it to a third reading.
The Majority Leader, Sunday Ojezele, moved the motion for the House to resolve into the Committee of the Whole to consider the bill.
Following its consideration, the House reverted to plenary and passed the bill.
Mr Idaiye subsequently directed the clerk to transmit a clean copy of the bill to Governor Monday Okpebholo for assent.
In a related development, the House received a message from Governor Okpebholo seeking confirmation of Abbas Suleiman as the state’s auditor-general.
Mr Idaiye referred the nomination to the Committee on Rules, Business and Government House for consideration and directed it to report back to the House within two weeks.
Meanwhile, consideration of three other bills was deferred to a later date.
They include a bill seeking to prohibit unauthorised removal and vandalism of metal structures, fittings and public infrastructure, while regulating scrap metal dealers.
Others seek to repeal the Edo State Traditional Medicine Board Law, 2026, and the Edo State Roads Funds Board Law, 2025.
The proposed roads fund legislation seeks to establish the Edo State Roads Fund and Board.
It is also intended to provide funding for managing, planning, rehabilitating, constructing, reconstructing and maintaining Class C and D roads.
The proposed fund will also support the rehabilitation of Class B roads across the state. The House subsequently adjourned sitting until 7 December, 2026.
